entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The World Organization of the Scout Movement (WOSM) is an international scouting organization founded in 1922 in Geneva, Switzerland, at the behest of Robert Baden-Powell, the founder of the Boy Scouts. This organization has played a crucial role in promoting youth education, global citizenship, and community service through the principles of scouting, which emphasize personal development, teamwork, and outdoor skills. It has expanded to include over 170 member organizations worldwide, representing approximately 50 million scouts across diverse cultures and regions.

The establishment of WOSM followed the successful first World Scout Jamboree held in London in 1920, where scouting was recognized as a global movement. This event catalyzed the formation of international connections and led to the creation of a structured organization that could oversee and promote scouting activities globally. WOSM also introduced key initiatives such as the World Scout Conference and the World Scout Moot, which foster ongoing collaboration among member organizations and enhance the scouting experience for youth.

The legacy of the World Organization of the Scout Movement is evident in its enduring impact on youth development and community engagement. Scouting has inspired generations of young people to participate in civic activities, embrace leadership roles, and develop a sense of global solidarity. The principles established by WOSM have influenced various youth organizations and educational programs, contributing to a broader understanding of global citizenship and personal responsibility.

As Baden-Powell once said, 'The spirit is there in every boy; it has to be discovered and brought to light.' This sentiment encapsulates the essence of scouting, which continues to resonate with millions around the world, underlining the organization's significant role in shaping active, responsible citizens for the future.
